questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The couple / preferred to walk / until the last house / of the town.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ‘3’ i.e. until the last house.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase 'until the last house' is incorrect in this context.
 
 
• The correct phrase should be **'up to the last house.'**
 
 
 
• The other segments are grammatically correct.
 
 
• **'The couple'** correctly refers to two people acting together.
 
• **'Preferred to walk'** correctly indicates their choice of activity.
 
• **'Of the town'** correctly indicates the location in question.
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: *The couple preferred to walk up to the last house of the town.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Using 'until' often implies a continuation of action up to a point in time, while 'up to' is more appropriate for physical distances or locations.
 
 
• **Example:** *We walked up to the park entrance.*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Passengers started behaving / violent when / they were asked / to leave the bus station.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ‘2’ i.e. violent when.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase 'violent when' is incorrect in this context.
 
 
• The correct phrase should be **'violently when.'**
 
• This is because 'violently' is the adverb that correctly modifies the verb 'behaving.'
 
 
 
• The other segments are grammatically correct:
 
 
• **'Passengers started behaving'** correctly sets the subject and verb phrase.
 
• **'they were asked'** correctly indicates the action done to the passengers.
 
• **'to leave the bus station'** correctly completes the action that the passengers were asked to do.
 
 

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *Passengers started behaving violently when they were asked to leave the bus station.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Adverbs often end in '-ly' and are used to modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs, providing more information about how an action is performed.
 
 
• **Example:** *She sang beautifully.*

questions.question: Select the sentence in the future tense.

options.text: I could be twenty five next Sunday.
I should be twenty five next Sunday.
I have been twenty five next Sunday.
I will be twenty five next Sunday.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is ‘4’ i.e. I will be twenty five next Sunday.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence 'I will be twenty five next Sunday' is in the future tense.
 
 
• The use of **'will be'** indicates an event that is certain to happen in the future.
 
 
 
• The other options are not in the future tense:
 
 
• **Option 1:** 'I could be twenty five next Sunday' uses 'could,' which indicates possibility but not a certain future event.
 
• **Option 2:** 'I should be twenty five next Sunday' uses 'should,' which indicates obligation or expectation, not a certain future event.
 
• **Option 3:** 'I have been twenty five next Sunday' is grammatically incorrect because it mixes present perfect tense with a future time reference.
 
 

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Future tense in English can be formed using 'will' followed by the base form of the verb.
 
 
• **Example:** *She will arrive tomorrow.*

questions.question:

questions.solution:

• **Option 3:** 'held down with' implies being physically restrained or burdened, which is not appropriate here.
 
• **Option 4:** 'looked down with' implies viewing with disapproval or disdain but is not idiomatically correct.
 
 

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *I am fed up with her complaints.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Idioms like 'fed up with' are used to express specific feelings or situations in a figurative manner.
 
 
• **Example:** *She is fed up with the constant noise.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

The little boy cried with pain __when he burnt__ his fingers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ‘1’ i.e. No substitution required.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase 'when he burnt his fingers' is correct and does not require substitution.
 
 
• The past tense 'burnt' matches with the past tense 'cried,' maintaining the grammatical consistency of the sentence.
 
 
 
• The other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **Option 2:** 'when he burns his fingers' uses present tense 'burns,' which is inconsistent with the past tense 'cried.'
 
• **Option 3:** 'while he burn his fingers' is grammatically incorrect because 'burn' should be 'burns' for the present tense or 'burned/burnt' in the past tense.
 
• **Option 4:** 'as he burning his fingers' is grammatically incorrect because it is missing an auxiliary verb and should be 'as he was burning his fingers.'
 
 

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *The little boy cried with pain when he burnt his fingers.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Maintaining verb tense consistency in a sentence is crucial for clarity and grammatical accuracy.
 
 
• **Example:** She laughed when she heard the joke.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

__This is best book__ for children to read.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ‘3’ i.e. This is the best book.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The phrase 'This is the best book' is the most appropriate option because 'the best' is the superlative form of 'good,' which is needed here to indicate that this book stands out as the best among all.
 
• The other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **Option 1:** 'This is good book' has a missing article 'a' before 'good,' which makes it grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Option 2:** 'This is very good book' also lacks the article 'a' and doesn't convey the superlative degree needed to indicate this book is outstanding among others.
 
• **Option 4:** 'This is very best book' is incorrect because 'very' should not be used directly before a superlative adjective.
 
 

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: *This is the best book for children to read.*
